How much each source's share of electricity changed between two years

Source: R/share_change.R
share_change.Rd

For every country and source in data, finds the share of electricity from that source in from and in to, the change in percentage points, and the average change per year. A percentage point is the difference between two percentages: a fall from 79% to 43% is a fall of 36 points.

Usage

share_change(data, from, to)

Arguments

data

A data frame with the same columns as electricity_mix, usually electricity_mix itself.

from

The start year.

to

The end year. Must be later than from.

Value

A data frame with one row per country and source, and columns:

country

Country name, or "World".

source

Source of electricity.

from_share

Percentage of electricity from the source in from. Missing if that year was not reported.

to_share

Percentage of electricity from the source in to. Missing if that year was not reported.

change

Change from from to to, in percentage points. Negative values are falls. Missing when either year is missing.

change_per_year

Average change per year, in percentage points.

result

The result in words, written to follow the country name.

Examples

changes <- share_change(electricity_mix, from = 2005, to = 2025)

dplyr::filter(changes, country == "Australia", source == "coal")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   country   source from_share to_share change change_per_year result            
#>   <chr>     <fct>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>           <dbl> <chr>             
#> 1 Australia coal         79.3     42.7  -36.6           -1.83 got 42.7% of its …
# Coal's share of Australia's electricity fell by about 37 points

dplyr::filter(changes, country == "Indonesia", source == "coal")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   country   source from_share to_share change change_per_year result            
#>   <chr>     <fct>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>           <dbl> <chr>             
#> 1 Indonesia coal         39.0       NA     NA              NA has no coal data …
# Indonesia's data end in 2024, so its change cannot be measured
